key_insight: Represent long video frames as a question-conditioned graph and select a compact, informative subset via graph reasoning so multimodal LLMs can answer long-horizon embodied questions more accurately and efficiently.
problem_solved: MLLMs degrade when fed many redundant or irrelevant frames from long videos; the paper addresses how to compactly summarize long-horizon visual memory while preserving temporal and relational cues needed for embodied video question answering.
method: Build a graph where nodes are candidate frames (or glimpses) and edges encode temporal/semantic relations; condition node scoring on the question and agent context.
Use graph-based reasoning (e.g., a lightweight GNN or attention over the graph) to rank and select a small, diverse subset of frames that maximize relevance and coverage.
Feed the selected frames (and their relations) into a multimodal LLM or downstream QA module to produce answers with lower compute and higher accuracy.
impact: Enables scalable, accurate long-video understanding for embodied agents by reducing input redundancy and preserving relational context—improving both efficiency and interpretability for practitioners building multimodal agents.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: long video → frame embedding → frame graph → selection → MLLM answering
Graph visualization: nodes as frames with edge types (temporal/semantic) and highlighted selected nodes
Before/after comparison chart: accuracy vs. number of frames (showing improved accuracy and lower compute with FocusGraph)
Icon set: robot/agent, clock/timeline, neural graph, and a question mark to denote embodied QA
paper_title: FocusGraph: Graph-Structured Frame Selection for Embodied Long Video Question Answering
paper_authors: Tatiana Zemskova, Solomon Andryushenko, Ilya Obrubov, Viktoriia Khoruzhaia, Ekaterina Eroshenko
